correctness.rationale: For a vertex in part Xi, the open-neighborhood label sum is exactly total weight minus the Xi weight, and a positive vertex has a positive neighbor exactly when positive support meets another part. Starting from all labelings supported on at least two parts, the only Roman {2} failure at Xi is a mixed Xi assignment with outside weight exactly one. Two such bad events intersect only in a weight-two labeling with one label-one vertex in each of two non-singleton parts, and no three bad events intersect. This proves the inclusion-exclusion formula. A fresh independent enumeration through order seven matched every coefficient for all 37 complete multipartite isomorphism types tested; the arbitrary-order proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The full weight distribution is a natural strengthening of a previously studied domination parameter: it records all feasible configurations rather than only the minimum, supports exact counting questions, and exposes the precise partwise obstruction. This is more than a known-table recomputation because the polynomial follows from a new all-labeling characterization.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph, total Roman {2}-dominating labelings are characterized exactly by positive support in at least two parts and outside-part weight at least two for every zero-containing part; this yields the stated closed weight enumerator for all feasible labelings, with the known minimum formula as a corollary.
limitations: The theorem is restricted to connected complete multipartite graphs and the standard total Roman {2} rule.
The minimum-weight corollary is prior-published and is not the originality basis.
The independent finite replay through order seven is corroborative; the proof is all-order.
A differently phrased non-indexed enumeration of total Roman {2}-dominating functions on complete multipartite graphs could exist.
